question.text: A gaseous compound of nitrogen and oxygen is paramagnetic in nature. When it is cooled below  <math><mn>0</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>  its molecular mass increases and paramagnetism is lost. The behaviour is reversed on heating. The compound is

solution.text: <math><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math>  is paramagnetic because of unpaired electron. On cooling  <math><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math>  below  <math><mn>0</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> , it  dimerises to  <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></math>  which does not have any unpaired electrons. Hence, no paramagnetism is show by the dimer,  <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></math> .
